title: Trump Pledges New 'AI Force' and Top Advisor as Administration Rejects Strict Tech Rules
snippet: President Donald Trump announced plans to appoint a new 'AI czar' and create a dedicated 'AI force,' doubling down on his stance against heavy government regulation of artificial intelligence.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump signaled a renewed push to champion American technology over the weekend, announcing plans to appoint a new artificial intelligence advisor and establish a dedicated "AI force."

Posting on Truth Social on Saturday, Trump offered few concrete details about how either initiative would be structured or funded. However, he made clear that his administration intends to foster industry growth rather than restrict it with new federal mandates.

"We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry," Trump wrote, asserting that existing legal frameworks are sufficient to handle bad actors. "Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows! However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System."

A Regulatory Divide in Washington

The announcement comes as lawmakers on Capitol Hill express heightened concern over the potential risks posed by rapid AI advancements, ranging from economic disruption to existential safety threats. Earlier this month, former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon sounded alarms, noting that many leading developers genuinely fear advanced AI could pose extreme risks to humanity within the decade.

Trump has consistently dismissed such alarms, aligning himself with prominent tech leaders who argue that preemptive rules would stifle American innovation. Should Trump proceed with the appointment, it would mark his second "AI czar." Venture capitalist David Sacks previously held the role before stepping down in the spring to transition into an external advisory capacity.

Sacks has echoed Trump's light-touch approach, arguing at a recent Politico event that AI developers should face liability for product harm through existing civil courts rather than navigating new federal bureaucracies.

Global Competition Drives Policy Push

The administration's stance is heavily influenced by the escalating technological rivalry between the United States and China. Both superpowers view artificial intelligence as a cornerstone of future economic prosperity and military dominance. Trump and Silicon Valley allies frequently argue that imposing strict safeguards on domestic companies would hand a decisive advantage to Chinese competitors.

The announcement arrives just days ahead of a high-stakes bilateral meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. As part of the broader diplomatic push, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is scheduled to meet with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng at JPMorgan Chase headquarters in New York to discuss trade, economic policy, and AI security protocols.
